title: 1,800+ Student Visas Revoked at 280 Colleges; SEVIS Terminations Widespread
synopsis: Beginning in late March 2025, the Trump administration conducted a sweeping, largely unexplained mass revocation of international student visas and SEVIS status terminations. Secretary of State Rubio initially acknowledged revoking approximately 300 visas; an AP review as of April 15 found at least 1,024 students at 160 institutions affected. Inside Higher Ed's tracking database grew to over 1,800 students at 280+ colleges across 45 states and D.C. by late April. Universities reported that the federal government provided no reasons for most terminations; some students were targeted for pro-Palestine protest activity, others for minor criminal charges such as a desk-appearance ticket. The University of California system totaled 76 affected students. At least 290 students filed in 65 separate lawsuits; the administration announced April 25 it would restore all terminated SEVIS statuses pending further review, then continued targeted revocations. AI-assisted social media screening was used to identify targets.

title: Bears Ears and Grand Staircase Shrunk 90% in Utah Land Grab
synopsis: On July 13, 2026, Trump signed proclamations under the Antiquities Act reducing Bears Ears National Monument from approximately 1.36 million acres to 121,096 acres — a 91% cut — and Grand Staircase-Escalante from 1.87 million acres to 181,541 acres — a 90% cut — removing nearly 3 million combined acres of protected land. Both monuments contain ancient cliff dwellings, petroglyphs, and coal and uranium deposits coveted by industry. Trump had taken similar actions in 2017 that Biden reversed. Critics called it a giveaway to mining and energy interests over sacred Native American lands.

title: Clean Power Plan Successor Rules Proposed for Full Repeal
synopsis: On June 11, 2025, EPA Administrator Zeldin proposed repealing all greenhouse gas emission standards for fossil fuel-fired power plants under Section 111 of the Clean Air Act, including the Biden-era 'Clean Power Plan 2.0' finalized in May 2024. The proposal argued that GHG emissions from power plants 'do not contribute significantly to dangerous air pollution,' a reversal of decades of EPA scientific findings. EPA's own regulatory impact analysis projected $19 billion in compliance cost savings from 2026–2047 under 3% discount rates, but did not calculate the climate damage costs. The EPA also proposed repealing Mercury and Air Toxics Standards (MATS) amendments that were forcing coal plant shutdowns.

title: Coal Plant Lifeline: DOE Emergency Orders Keep Dying Plants Online
synopsis: Beginning May 23, 2025, Energy Secretary Chris Wright invoked emergency authority under Section 202(c) of the Federal Power Act to force the J.H. Campbell coal plant in Michigan — which was scheduled to permanently close — to remain operational, over the objections of both the grid operator and the plant's owner, Consumers Energy. The plant had been in a multi-year retirement process approved in 2022. CNN reported the move would cost Midwest ratepayers in 15 states tens of millions of dollars. The DOE subsequently issued additional emergency coal orders for plants in Indiana, Washington state, Colorado (Craig Station, December 30, 2025), and others. The regional grid operator MISO said it had not requested the Michigan extension.

title: Endangered Species Act 'Harm' Definition Rescinded, Opening Habitats
synopsis: On July 10–11, 2026, the Interior and Commerce Departments finalized a rule rescinding the regulatory definition of 'harm' under the Endangered Species Act (ESA), effective September 14, 2026. For 50 years, 'harm' had included habitat modification or degradation that kills or injures wildlife by impairing essential behaviors — a protection upheld by the Supreme Court in 1995. The new rule means oil drilling, mining, logging, and development can proceed in critical habitats so long as animals are not directly killed. A separate rule finalized July 17, 2026 required economic impact analyses when designating critical habitat. CNN called it 'reversing 50 years of environmental law.' Environmentalists warned it could drive multiple species toward extinction.

title: Wildfire Policy Failure: Prescribed Burns Halved, Four Firefighters Dead
synopsis: In 2025, the U.S. Forest Service — having lost 16% of its workforce (5,860 staff) under DOGE cuts — reduced hazardous fuel treatment by 1.5 million acres compared to 2024, including cutting prescribed burns nearly in half from over 1.6 million acres to roughly 900,000 acres. Agriculture Secretary Rollins and Interior Secretary Burgum then ordered a sweeping 'full suppression' policy for 2026, abandoning decades of science-backed managed fire strategies. On June 27, 2026, four federal firefighters died when the Snyder Fire in Colorado overran their position. Trump created the U.S. Wildland Fire Service by secretarial order — pulling 3,900 Interior firefighters from six agencies — without congressional approval. By August 2026, millions of acres were burning across the West under unprecedented drought conditions.

title: Big Beautiful Bill Kills IRA Clean Energy Tax Credits
synopsis: On July 4, 2025, Trump signed the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (P.L. 119-21), which repealed or sharply restricted nearly every clean energy tax credit enacted under the 2022 Inflation Reduction Act. The EV consumer tax credits (Sections 30D, 25E, 45W) were repealed for vehicles acquired after September 30, 2025; the Residential Clean Energy Credit (solar, geothermal; Section 25D) was repealed for installations after December 31, 2025. The Joint Committee on Taxation projected the law would reduce federal clean energy expenditures by roughly $267 billion in consumer credits and over $48 billion in advanced manufacturing credits through 2033. Wind and solar projects were made ineligible for clean electricity investment and production tax credits unless entering service before January 1, 2028.

title: Title IX Reverted to 2020 Rules, Transgender Student Protections Stripped
synopsis: On January 20, 2025, Trump signed an executive order declaring only two biological sexes exist and directing all federal agencies to reinterpret sex-based statutes accordingly, explicitly rescinding 11 Biden-era Title IX guidance documents protecting LGBTQ+ students. On January 31, the Department of Education issued a Dear Colleague letter to all schools confirming immediate enforcement of the 2020 Title IX regulations — which exclude gender identity from sex discrimination protections — effective retroactively for all open investigations. On February 5, Trump signed an additional executive order directing the DOJ to enforce a ban on transgender girls and women in female school sports under Title IX, threatening federal funding cuts for noncompliance. Schools in 26 states that had already reverted under prior court orders were joined by every other U.S. institution, eliminating transgender bathroom access, pronoun policies, and harassment protections at federally funded schools nationwide.

title: USDA/RFK Dietary Guidelines Politicized; NIH Nutrition Research Gutted
synopsis: In March 2025, Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins and RFK Jr. announced a 'line-by-line review' of the 2025 Dietary Guidelines Advisory Committee's science report, with Kennedy pledging guidelines as short as four pages — compared to the prior 164-page document — potentially contradicting scientific consensus on saturated fats, seed oils, and red meat. The NIH's lead ultra-processed food researcher resigned in April 2025 after 21 years, citing fear of censorship. The Trump budget proposed cutting NIH nutrition research funding while also eliminating the CDC's National Center for Chronic Disease Prevention and Health Promotion ($1.4 billion annual budget). Scientists and CSPI condemned the MAHA Commission's strategy report for including fake citations and pseudoscientific claims, while the administration canceled over $1 billion in local food funding and terminated NIH grants covering nutrition and diet-related disease research.

title: Pentagon DEI Purge: 188 Positions Abolished, Advisory Committee Disbanded
synopsis: On January 27, 2025, Trump signed Executive Order 14185 directing Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to abolish every DEI office within the Department of Defense, including all sub-offices, programs, and initiatives. According to a Government Accountability Office report released April 17, 2025, the DOD had cut or restructured 188 DEI-related civilian and military positions since early 2024. The congressionally chartered Defense Advisory Committee on Diversity and Inclusion was disbanded, and a Pentagon task force was created in February 2025 to oversee and certify the complete elimination of DEI activity across all military branches. By March 1, 2025, the task force certified no DEI goals remained in organizational composition, academic admissions, or career fields across any branch.

title: Penn $175M Research Halted; Stanford 82 Grants Cut; Universities Targeted
synopsis: In March 2025, the Trump administration issued stop-work orders on $175 million in federally contracted research across seven schools at the University of Pennsylvania, citing the university's 2022 allowance of a transgender athlete on the women's swim team — even though Penn stated it was already complying with the new Title IX rules. The halted contracts covered research on preventing hospital infections, drug screening against viruses, quantum computing, chemical warfare defenses, and student loan programs. Stanford University reported 82 federally supported grant terminations by September 2025, totaling $41.2 million. Dozens of other research universities — including Harvard, Columbia, Penn, and institutions across 26 states — faced NIH and NSF grant terminations as the administration used research funding as political leverage in a broader campaign against universities.

title: Big Beautiful Bill Medicaid Cuts: 10 Million Lose Coverage
synopsis: The One Big Beautiful Bill Act (P.L. 119-21), signed by Trump on July 4, 2025, contains approximately $840 billion in Medicaid cuts over ten years. The Congressional Budget Office (CBO) estimated on July 21, 2025 that the law's health provisions would leave 10 million more Americans without insurance by 2034. The law's community engagement (work) requirements alone — which mandate that able-bodied, non-elderly adults prove employment, education, or community service to retain Medicaid — will reduce federal Medicaid outlays by $325.6 billion and cause 4.8 million people to lose coverage by 2034. An additional 1.3 million people with both Medicaid and Medicare would lose their Medicaid coverage. Democrats and health advocacy groups called the cuts the largest reduction to Medicaid in the program's 60-year history.

title: ACA Navigator Program Slashed 90%, Enrollment Rules Tightened
synopsis: On February 14, 2025 — the day after RFK Jr. was sworn in as HHS secretary — the Trump administration announced it would cut the ACA Navigator program from $98 million to $10 million annually, a reduction of $360 million over four years. Navigators are community-based organizations that help low-income and uninsured Americans enroll in ACA marketplace plans; in 2024 they served roughly 4.6 million people with counseling and enrollment assistance. The administration justified the cut by claiming navigators enrolled only 0.6% of marketplace selections at a cost of $1,061 per enrollment. In June 2025, CMS also finalized rules shortening the open enrollment window to end December 15 (one month earlier) and eliminating the monthly special enrollment period for those below 150% of the federal poverty line, which had been created to help the most vulnerable sign up year-round.

title: SNAP Food Stamp Cuts: 2.7 Million Lose Benefits Under OBBBA
synopsis: The One Big Beautiful Bill Act enacted on July 4, 2025 imposed the largest cuts to the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) in the program's history, reducing federal SNAP spending by over $280 billion over ten years. CBO analyses released in August 2025 found that expanded work requirements will cause 2.4 million fewer Americans to receive benefits in an average month, including parents of dependent children newly subject to work mandates for the first time. An additional 300,000 people will lose benefits beginning in 2028 when states are required to share benefit costs, with some states expected to leave the program entirely. A cap on Thrifty Food Plan updates will reduce the average monthly benefit from a projected $227 to $213 by 2034. Groups most at risk include veterans, people experiencing homelessness, and young adults aging out of foster care.

title: Medication Abortion Under Siege: FDA Review, Comstock Threat
synopsis: In May 2025, HHS Secretary RFK Jr. directed the FDA to launch a safety review of mifepristone — the first medication in a two-drug regimen used in 63% of U.S. abortions — which experts warned could lead to tighter telehealth restrictions, mandatory in-person prescriptions, or removal from pharmacy shelves. As of July 2025, 12 states had total abortion bans and nine states explicitly banned telehealth-provided medication abortion. The Trump Justice Department was also weighing a broader interpretation of the 1873 Comstock Act that could ban mailing abortion pills nationwide regardless of state law. Texas in September 2025 passed a law allowing private citizens to sue physicians, manufacturers, and distributors from outside the state who mail abortion medication into Texas — a direct attack on blue-state shield laws. Louisiana grand-juried a New York doctor in January 2025 for providing telehealth abortions to a patient in Louisiana.

title: Title X Family Planning Freeze: 879 Clinics, 834,000 Patients at Risk
synopsis: On March 31, 2025, the Trump administration froze Title X family planning funding for 16 of 86 grantees, withholding more than $65 million that had been earmarked for contraception, STI testing, and cancer screenings at clinics serving low-income and uninsured patients. All nine Planned Parenthood federation affiliates with Title X grants were affected, as were seven other nonprofit grantees. KFF estimated 879 clinics in 23 states — 24% of all Title X clinics — were impacted, and up to 834,000 people could lose access to Title X-funded care. HHS cited unspecified civil rights violations and Trump's executive order barring benefits to undocumented immigrants but refused to detail the alleged infractions. By late April 2025, dozens of clinics had begun closing. Title X serves 2.8 million clients annually across nearly 4,000 clinics, with 83% of patients having family incomes at or below 250% of the federal poverty level.

title: Drug Pricing EOs: Biden Pilot Programs Killed, MFN Order Has No Teeth
synopsis: On January 20, 2025, Trump rescinded Executive Order 14087 — Biden's 2022 order directing HHS to develop new models to lower drug costs for Medicare and Medicaid patients, including a proposed $2 monthly cap on generic drugs. While the IRA's $35 insulin cap and $2,000 annual out-of-pocket cap remained intact as statutory law, the cancellation ended three CMS Innovation Center pilot programs before they could be implemented. On May 12, 2025, Trump signed Executive Order 14297 directing drugmakers to align U.S. prices with the lowest prices in comparable developed nations ('most favored nation' pricing); pharma stocks rose on the announcement as analysts and legal experts questioned how it could be enforced. Congressional Research Service analysis noted the order lacked defined legal authority and could conflict with existing IRA drug negotiation provisions. No major price reductions had materialized from the MFN order by August 2025.

title: Rural Hospital Closures: 300+ at Risk from $840B Medicaid Cuts
synopsis: A June 2025 analysis by the Cecil G. Sheps Center for Health Services Research found that over 300 financially struggling rural hospitals were at heightened risk of closure, service reductions, or ending inpatient care due to the OBBBA's Medicaid cuts. Nearly half of all rural hospitals were already operating in the red before the law's enactment, and the cuts were projected to drain $1.8 billion from rural hospital net revenues with a 15% Medicaid reduction. The law included a $50 billion, five-year Rural Health Transformation Program, but Health Affairs analysis found it was not required to flow to rural hospitals, was run by CMS Administrator Mehmet Oz with broad discretion, and expired after five years while Medicaid cuts were permanent. By early 2026, rural hospitals in Nebraska, North Carolina, New Hampshire, Minnesota, Virginia, and Oklahoma were closing services, with INTEGRIS Health citing a projected $130 million loss.

title: Liberation Day: Trump's Global Tariff Shock Rattles World Markets
synopsis: On April 2, 2025, President Trump declared a national economic emergency and announced sweeping tariffs from the Rose Garden — a 34% rate on China, 20% on the European Union, 24% on Japan, and a 10% baseline on virtually all other nations, branding it 'Liberation Day.' Global markets reacted immediately: Japan's Nikkei dropped nearly 4%, Hong Kong's Hang Seng fell 1.5%, and U.S. Dow futures were down 2.5% pre-market. JPMorgan analysts warned the tariffs would impose a $660 billion annual tax increase on Americans, raise CPI by 2%, and likely push the U.S. and global economies into recession in 2025 — raising their recession probability estimate from 40% to 60%. EU Commission President Ursula von der Leyen called it 'a major blow to the world economy' with 'dire' consequences for millions of people.

title: 25% Auto Tariffs Devastate Ford, GM, Stellantis: $108B in Costs
synopsis: Trump's 25% tariffs on imported vehicles took effect April 3, 2025, with 25% tariffs on auto parts set to follow by May 3. The Center for Automotive Research calculated the tariffs would increase costs for all US automakers by $107.7 billion in 2025 — $41.9 billion for Ford, GM, and Stellantis alone. Goldman Sachs estimated new vehicle prices would rise $2,000-$4,000; Cox Automotive projected a $6,000 increase for fully imported vehicles. Stellantis idled factories in Canada and Mexico making Chrysler and Jeep vehicles, laying off 900 US workers; Jaguar Land Rover suspended all US exports; Porsche halted European shipments. Analyst firm Telemetry projected upward of 2 million fewer vehicles sold annually in the US and Canada. Trump partially softened the tariffs April 29 by offering credits for domestically assembled vehicles, but core levies remained.

title: $6.6 Trillion Wiped From Markets in Historic Post-Tariff Crash
synopsis: The two trading days following Trump's Liberation Day tariff announcement — April 3 and 4, 2025 — produced the largest two-day S&P 500 market value destruction on record, surpassing even the COVID-19 crash of March 2020. The S&P 500 lost approximately $5 trillion in market cap by Reuters' count, with WSJ reporting a total of $6.6 trillion erased. The Dow Jones fell 1,679 points on April 3 alone, its biggest single-day drop since June 2020; the Nasdaq confirmed it entered a bear market, falling more than 20% from its December 2024 peak. Apple lost $315 billion in market cap in a single day — the second-largest single-stock decline on record. By the 100-day mark of Trump's second term, over $6.5 trillion had been wiped from public company valuations, making it the worst stock market start to any presidential term since Gerald Ford in 1974.

title: Tariff-Driven Grocery Inflation Hits Fastest Pace Since 2022
synopsis: By August 2025, US grocery prices had risen at their fastest monthly pace since 2022, with the food-at-home CPI component jumping 0.6% in a single month, up 2.7% year-over-year, driven in part by Trump's tariffs on imports from China, steel, aluminum, and other nations. Coffee prices surged 20.9% year-over-year as of August 2025; uncooked beef steaks rose 16.6%; apples climbed 9.6%; bananas 6.6%. Yale University's Budget Lab estimated food prices would rise 3.4% in the short run and remain 2.5% higher long-run under Trump's tariff levels. A Federal Reserve analysis found tariffs accounted for roughly 0.5 percentage points of annualized headline PCE inflation in June-August 2025 and explained 10.9% of annual PCE inflation for the 12 months ending August 2025. Trump had campaigned on a pledge to lower grocery prices.

title: Section 232 Steel and Aluminum Tariffs Doubled to 50% in June 2025
synopsis: On June 3, 2025, Trump signed a proclamation under Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962 doubling steel and aluminum tariffs from 25% to 50%, effective June 4 — on top of the February 2025 expansion that had already removed all country exemptions and raised aluminum tariffs to 25% globally. The 50% rate applied to all countries except the UK, which was held at 25% under the US-UK Economic Prosperity Deal. In August 2025, the Commerce Department added over 400 product codes to the tariff scope, including household appliances. By year-end 2025, US steel imports had fallen 21% compared to 2024 — from $31.6 billion to $24.8 billion — while aluminum imports fell 5% to $17.5 billion. The cumulative Section 232 tariff actions in 2025, combined with IEEPA-based universal tariffs, produced the most restrictive US trade policy since before World War II.

title: '90 Deals in 90 Days' Collapses: Only 2 Deals Reached by Deadline
synopsis: When Trump announced the 90-day tariff pause on April 9, 2025, White House trade adviser Peter Navarro boasted of '90 deals in 90 days,' and Trump himself claimed at his 100-day mark to have struck deals with '200 countries.' By the July 9 deadline, only two formal agreements had been reached — a partial framework with the United Kingdom and a preliminary deal with Vietnam. Trump then extended his own 'final' deadline to August 1, declaring 'no extensions will be granted,' only to extend it again. By July 9, 2025, CNN reported just three deals (UK, Vietnam, and China's partial 90-day tariff reduction), far short of the promised comprehensive restructuring of global trade. Foreign officials across 10 countries told Politico that negotiations were bogged down. The EU ultimately settled for a 15% tariff deal just days before August 1, with France immediately declaring it needed renegotiation.

title: EO 14168: 'Two Sexes Only' Order Rewrites Federal Law
synopsis: Executive Order 14168, 'Defending Women from Gender Ideology Extremism and Restoring Biological Truth to the Federal Government,' signed January 20, 2025, declared it official federal policy to 'recognize two sexes, male and female' defined by 'immutable biological classification' at conception. The order directed all federal agencies to apply this definition when interpreting statutes, regulations, and guidance; replace the term 'gender' with 'sex' on all federal documents; remove gender-identity fields from agency forms; and direct the attorney general to issue guidance limiting the scope of Bostock v. Clayton County to narrow hiring and promotions decisions, specifically excluding its application to Title IX and Section 1557 of the Affordable Care Act. The order rescinded five prior executive orders including EOs 13988, 14004, 14020, 14021, and 14075, dissolved the White House Gender Policy Council, and required a proposed bill to codify the definitions within 30 days. It applied to passports, visas, federal employee records, prison housing, and all federally funded entities including contractors, affecting an estimated 314,000 LGBTQ federal employees and contractors.

title: LGBTQ Federal Employees Targeted in DEI Purge and Firings
synopsis: Beginning January 20, 2025, Trump's executive orders on DEI and 'gender ideology' immediately placed employees whose roles involved 'promoting gender ideology' on paid administrative leave with computer access cut off, and at least six EOs directly targeted LGBTQ people in the federal workforce. The Williams Institute estimated approximately 314,000 LGBTQ employees of the federal government, USPS, and federal contractors were exposed to displacement. An OPM memo in early February directed agencies to prohibit employee resource groups promoting 'DEIA initiatives,' and OPM opened a tipline for workers to report colleagues involved in DEI activities — drawing comparisons to the 1950s 'Lavender Scare.' Trump also rescinded a nearly 60-year-old executive order (EO 11246) on January 21, 2025 prohibiting discrimination by federal contractors, removing protections for roughly 100,000 LGBTQ contractor employees. The Department of Homeland Security announced it would allow its agents to conduct surveillance based solely on a target's gender identity or sexual orientation. On March 26, 2025, a class-action complaint was filed before the Merit Systems Protection Board on behalf of fired federal DEI employees.

title: State-Level Anti-Trans Surge: 600+ Bills Follow Federal Lead
synopsis: In 2025, the ACLU documented more than 600 anti-transgender bills introduced at the U.S. state level — a new record, exceeding the 500-plus bills introduced in both 2023 and 2024 — directly emboldened by Trump's federal executive orders on sex definitions and gender-affirming care. By December 2025, 29 states had enacted at least one law restricting transgender youth healthcare, sports participation, bathroom access, or pronoun use in schools, and 348,400 transgender youth aged 13–17 lived in states that had banned them from bathrooms aligned with their gender identity. Twelve states enacted new bathroom bans in 2025 alone — including Georgia, Montana, Texas, and Wyoming. The Supreme Court's June 2025 ruling in U.S. v. Skrmetti upheld Tennessee's healthcare ban under the Equal Protection Clause, removing the primary constitutional barrier to state bans and triggering immediate enforcement in multiple states. By August 2025, at least eight major hospital systems in Democratic-led states had halted gender-affirming care for minors after Trump's administration sent subpoenas and publicly boasted about intimidating providers, leading 17 Democratic attorneys general to file suit on August 1, 2025.

title: RSF Press Freedom Index: US Drops to 57th, Behind Sierra Leone
synopsis: On May 2, 2025, Reporters Without Borders (RSF) published its annual World Press Freedom Index, ranking the United States 57th out of 180 countries — a decline of 2 places from 2024 and 13 places from 2023, placing the US one spot behind Sierra Leone. RSF noted 'an alarming deterioration in press freedom' under Trump's second term and cited 'an authoritarian shift in government,' including weaponized institutions, defunding of independent media, and sidelining of reporters. The US social indicator score dropped 28 places, and the economic indicator fell 14 points over two years. The Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) issued a simultaneous warning urging newsrooms to form a united front against the 'rising tide of threats.' The RSF noted that over 60% of journalists surveyed in Arizona, Florida, Nevada, and Pennsylvania said it was 'difficult to earn a living wage as a journalist.'

title: Trump Executive Order Mandates Proof of Citizenship to Register to Vote
synopsis: On March 25, 2025, Trump signed Executive Order 14248, directing the Election Assistance Commission — an independent bipartisan agency — to add documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to the national mail voter registration form. The order threatened to strip federal election funding from any state that refused to comply. An estimated 21.3 million eligible U.S. citizens (9% of voting-age citizens) lack readily available proof of citizenship, including a passport or REAL ID. Multiple federal courts issued preliminary injunctions blocking the order's key provisions; a permanent block on the citizenship-proof mandate was issued October 31, 2025, with a court ruling Trump lacks authority to unilaterally alter election procedures.

title: Trump Threatens to Deploy National Guard to 2026 Midterm Polling Places
synopsis: In a January 7, 2026 New York Times interview, Trump expressed regret that he had not directed the National Guard to seize voting machines after the 2020 election, signaling his intent to use military force around the 2026 midterms. Trump had already deployed the National Guard to at least four Democratic-led cities against the will of their governors in 2025, with courts issuing multiple injunctions. A February 2026 PBS News report revealed a 17-page draft executive order circulating among Trump allies that would declare a national emergency to take federal control over midterm elections, require hand-counting of ballots, and force voters to re-register with proof of citizenship. Trump publicly threatened on Truth Social: 'There will be Voter I.D. for the Midterm Elections, whether approved by Congress or not!' Legal experts said any troop deployment to polls would violate multiple federal statutes.

title: Trump EO Orders Ballots Must Be Received by Election Day, Threatens Funding to States
synopsis: Section 7 of Trump's March 25, 2025 Executive Order 14248 directed the Attorney General to sue any state that counted absentee or mail-in ballots received after Election Day, even if postmarked on or before Election Day — a practice used by millions of voters in numerous states. The EAC was directed to condition federal election funding on states adopting this hard Election Day receipt deadline. A federal judge in Boston issued a preliminary injunction on June 13, 2025, blocking the ballot-deadline provision along with the citizenship registration mandate, ruling Trump lacked authority to mandate changes to state election procedures. At least three states — Kansas, North Dakota, and Utah — separately passed legislation eliminating their mail ballot grace periods following the EO's political pressure.

title: Pentagon Retaliates Against Gen. Milley, Launches IG Investigation
synopsis: On January 29, 2025, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth revoked retired Gen. Mark Milley's personal security detail and suspended his security clearance, ordering the Pentagon Inspector General to investigate Milley's conduct and determine whether his four-star rank should be retroactively stripped. Milley had been on Iranian kill lists since 2020 after Trump's order to kill Qassem Soleimani — leaving him without protection against a documented threat. Senators condemned the revocation as placing Milley and his family in grave danger. Former Chief of Staff John Kelly and former Defense Secretary James Mattis were also subjected to retributive administrative actions, and a federal grand jury indicted John Bolton in October 2025 on charges of unlawful handling of classified information.

title: AG Bondi Creates 'Weaponization Working Group' Targeting Bragg, James, Smith
synopsis: On February 5, 2025, Attorney General Pam Bondi issued a memo titled 'Restoring the Integrity and Credibility of the Department of Justice,' creating a Weaponization Working Group specifically naming Manhattan DA Alvin Bragg, New York AG Letitia James, and former Special Counsel Jack Smith as subjects of investigation. The memo accused the prior DOJ of spending more than $50 million 'targeting' Trump and directed investigators to examine all federal cooperation with New York state legal actions against Trump. By August 2025, DOJ had convened a grand jury and subpoenaed James' office for documents. In October 2025, James was indicted by a Trump-installed loyalist prosecutor; a federal judge dismissed the case in November 2025, finding the prosecutor had been unlawfully appointed.

title: DOJ Drops Police Consent Decrees for Minneapolis, Louisville, Eight Other Cities
synopsis: On May 21, 2025, the DOJ Civil Rights Division — led by Harmeet Dhillon — announced it was dismissing pending lawsuits and proposed consent decrees against the Minneapolis and Louisville police departments, as well as closing investigations into six additional departments: Phoenix, Trenton, Memphis, Mount Vernon (NY), Oklahoma City, and Louisiana State Police. The Minneapolis and Louisville decrees had been negotiated following the police killings of George Floyd and Breonna Taylor respectively. Dhillon characterized the Biden-era investigations as relying on 'flawed methodologies' and 'wrongly equating statistical disparities with intentional discrimination.' Former DOJ Civil Rights Division chief Kristen Clarke called the rollback a 'patent disregard for our laws and the Constitution.'

title: DOJ Directs Investigations Into George Soros-Funded Progressive Prosecutors
synopsis: In May 2025, the DOJ Civil Rights Division opened an investigation into Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty over a policy directing prosecutors to consider racial disparities in plea negotiations. In September 2025, a DOJ senior official directed U.S. attorney's offices in at least seven states to prepare investigations into George Soros' Open Society Foundations on potential charges including material support for terrorism, arson, wire fraud, and racketeering — the directive following Trump and Vance publicly calling for Soros to be investigated. In May 2026, DOJ launched a civil rights probe into Fairfax County Commonwealth Attorney Steve Descano, who received over $600,000 from a Soros-funded PAC, over a policy of weighing immigration consequences in charging decisions.

title: Trump Threatens Insurrection Act Invocation Against Democratic Cities
synopsis: Beginning in October 2025, Trump repeatedly threatened to invoke the Insurrection Act of 1807 to deploy active-duty military troops into Chicago, Portland, and other Democratic-led cities over resistance to ICE operations. A federal judge in California had already ruled in September 2025 that the administration's deployment of active-duty troops to Los Angeles violated the Posse Comitatus Act of 1878. Senior White House aide Stephen Miller had been the leading internal proponent of invoking the Act, and officials shifted from debating whether to invoke it to how and when. Trump described anti-ICE protesters in Portland as committing 'pure insurrection,' while Illinois Gov. Pritzker accused Trump of deliberately manufacturing pretexts for military deployment against his political opponents.

title: Jack Smith Final Report: Evidence Was Sufficient to Convict Trump
synopsis: On January 14, 2025 — six days before Trump's inauguration — the Justice Department released Volume 1 of Special Counsel Jack Smith's 137-page final report on the election subversion investigation. Smith declared unequivocally that 'the admissible evidence was sufficient to obtain and sustain a conviction at trial' and that Trump had engaged in 'criminal efforts to retain power,' making 'specific and knowingly false claims of election fraud.' The report quoted Trump privately remarking after Biden appeared on TV 'Can you believe I lost to this f---ing guy?' and documented Trump berating Pence for being 'too honest.' Smith noted the only reason Trump escaped prosecution was DOJ's longstanding policy against prosecuting a sitting president — not the absence of evidence. Trump dismissed the report as the work of a 'lamebrain prosecutor.'

title: Trump Calls Putin's Ukraine Invasion 'Genius' and 'Savvy'
synopsis: On February 22, 2022, Trump declared on radio: 'I went in yesterday and there was a television screen, and I said, This is genius. Putin declares a big portion of Ukraine as independent.' He praised Putin as 'very savvy' for framing the invasion as a 'peacekeeping' operation. Although pre-dating his second term, the statements directly shaped his second administration's pro-Russia Ukraine posture — he repeatedly cited them in office to justify refusing to condemn Putin, and no retraction was ever issued. Rep. Liz Cheney responded: 'Former President Trump's adulation of Putin today — including calling him a genius — aids our enemies.'

title: Family Separation 2.0: 205,000 Children Lose a Parent to Deportation
synopsis: Unlike the border-based 'zero tolerance' separations of Trump's first term that affected roughly 5,000 children, the second term's family separations played out invisibly across U.S. communities. A July 2025 ICE directive rescinded Biden-era protections against detaining parents of U.S.-citizen children and abolished requirements to place detained parents near their minor children. The Brookings Institution estimated approximately 205,000 children — 71 percent of them U.S. citizens — had a parent detained by immigration officials as of May 2026; CNN identified over 100 U.S.-citizen children left stranded without parents by September 2025. ORR shared over 460,000 tips about unaccompanied children with ICE, leading to more than 12,000 arrests of child sponsors.

title: DOGE Attempts to Access Every American's IRS Tax Records
synopsis: Starting February 16, 2025, DOGE operative Gavin Kliger — a 25-year-old software engineer — arrived at IRS headquarters demanding broad access to a master database containing tax returns, addresses, Social Security numbers, income details, and child custody information for every taxpayer, business, and nonprofit in the country. Senior IRS executives pushed back, describing the request as a worst-case privacy scenario. A February 21 memorandum of understanding ultimately limited access to anonymized data only, after three weeks of internal standoffs. The episode revealed that DOGE had simultaneously deployed Kliger across OPM, USAID, and the State Department, essentially embedding a single operative as a data harvester across the entire federal government.

title: $TRUMP Memecoin Launched 3 Days Before Inauguration — $14B Peak, Suspected Insider Trading
synopsis: On January 17, 2025 — three days before his inauguration — Trump announced $TRUMP, a Solana-based memecoin distributed through Trump Organization affiliates CIC Digital LLC and Fight Fight Fight LLC, which retained 80% of the total 1 billion token supply. The coin's market cap surged to over $14 billion at its peak on January 20. A crypto wallet documented by Wired purchased $1.1 million in tokens within 90 seconds of Trump's announcement before the coin was indexed on exchanges, then made an estimated $85–$116 million in gains — suggesting insider knowledge. More than $2 billion in cumulative losses were suffered by retail investors who bought after the peak, while Trump-affiliated entities profited enormously from the coins they retained.

title: $MELANIA Memecoin Launches Inauguration Eve, Crashes $TRUMP 50% Instantly
synopsis: On January 19, 2025 — the eve of the inauguration — incoming First Lady Melania Trump launched the $MELANIA memecoin via her company MKT World LLC, just two days after Donald Trump's $TRUMP coin. The coin briefly reached a fully diluted market cap of over $5 billion, with the team retaining 35% of the 1 billion token supply on a 13-month unlock schedule. The launch immediately crashed $TRUMP by approximately 50%, from $72 to $44, as traders sold Trump coins to fund Melania purchases. A crypto personality publicly admitted to having known about $MELANIA in advance, and the simultaneous launch of two presidential family memecoins within 48 hours of taking office was condemned by ethics experts and prominent voices within the cryptocurrency industry as 'grifting at the expense of the crypto community.'

title: Musk Uses X to Publicly Expose SSA Data, Implying Fraud Without Evidence
synopsis: In February 2025, Musk posted Social Security Administration data directly on X, sharing figures about beneficiary age distributions drawn from SSA's Numident database — a master file of personally identifiable information for every American with a Social Security number. Musk implied massive fraud by suggesting that people over 100 were collecting benefits, posting: 'Maybe Twilight is real and there are a lot of vampires collecting Social Security.' Former SSA officials publicly explained that the Numident records were simply not updated with death records and had no correlation to actual payment records, calling Musk's interpretation 'just silly' and 'manipulative.' SSA Commissioner Michelle King had already resigned over DOGE's handling of the data; Musk was publicly broadcasting sensitive federal database contents sourced through unauthorized system access to justify further cuts.

title: Big Beautiful Bill Guts Medicaid: 10 Million Lose Coverage
synopsis: Trump signed the One Big Beautiful Bill Act on July 4, 2025, enacting the largest Medicaid rollback since the program's creation. The Congressional Budget Office projected the law would reduce federal Medicaid spending by $793 billion over 10 years and increase the uninsured population by 10.3 million by 2034. Key cuts included work requirements for 18.5 million expansion adults, six-month eligibility redeterminations instead of annual, and the elimination of ACA marketplace subsidies for immigrants. Combined with expiring enhanced ACA premium tax credits, CBO projected 16 million total additional uninsured Americans by 2034.

title: Medicaid Work Requirements Signed Into Law: 5–10 Million Face Disenrollment
synopsis: Section 44141 of the One Big Beautiful Bill, signed July 4, 2025, requires states to enforce 80-hours-per-month work requirements on Medicaid expansion adults beginning January 1, 2027, affecting an estimated 18.5 million enrollees. The Robert Wood Johnson Foundation modeled that between 4.9 and 10.1 million people would lose Medicaid coverage by 2028 depending on state implementation. Nebraska began early implementation on May 1, 2026. The CBO found that 4.8 million of those disenrolled would be working adults who simply fail to navigate complex monthly reporting systems — not people actually violating work requirements.

title: RFK Jr. Promotes Vitamins Over Vaccines During Measles Crisis
synopsis: HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. responded to the worst measles outbreak in 33 years by promoting vitamin A, cod liver oil, budesonide, and the antibiotic clarithromycin as alternatives to vaccination — recommendations doctors called dangerous misinformation. AP News reported that Kennedy had not been briefed in person by CDC infectious disease experts on the outbreak as late as March 21, 2025, weeks after the first child death. In May, Kennedy directed federal health agencies to search for 'new treatments' for measles including vitamins rather than issue a unified call for vaccination. His HHS simultaneously laid off approximately 10,000 federal health workers, disrupting CDC laboratory capacity and the FDA's bird flu testing infrastructure.

title: EPA Proposes Repealing Greenhouse Gas and Mercury Standards for Coal Plants
synopsis: On June 11, 2025, EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin announced proposals to repeal all greenhouse gas emission standards for power plants under Section 111 of the Clean Air Act and to roll back the 2024 Mercury and Air Toxics Standards, reverting mercury limits to 2012 baselines. EPA simultaneously granted 71 coal-fired power plants two-year exemptions from existing Mercury and Air Toxics Standards, more than any other industrial category. Zeldin called climate action 'a cult' and framed coal power as essential for AI data centers. Environmental groups said weakening mercury rules would increase exposure to a potent neurotoxin that impairs brain development in children across coal-producing and downwind states.

title: BLM Opens 250,000 Wyoming Acres Near Yellowstone and Grand Teton to Oil Drilling
synopsis: Interior Secretary Doug Burgum signed a secretarial order in February 2025 requiring BLM to prioritize reducing barriers to energy development on public lands and shorten permitting timelines from two years to 28 days under emergency procedures. The administration's 2025 Wyoming lease sales offered 45,804 acres near Yellowstone for oil and gas drilling, followed by a proposed 2026 auction of over 250,000 Wyoming acres, including more than 88,000 acres overlapping all three state-designated mule deer migration corridors and the pronghorn corridor adjacent to Grand Teton National Park. The Big Beautiful Bill additionally mandated that at least 50% of all industry-nominated public lands be made available for leasing, removing BLM's conservation-based discretion.

title: Endangered Species Act Protections Stripped from Lesser Prairie Chicken
synopsis: On February 26, 2026, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service formally delisted both population segments of the lesser prairie chicken from the Endangered Species Act, following Trump administration decisions to side with Texas, Oklahoma, and Kansas in lawsuits filed by the beef and petroleum industries. Federal protections had been vacated by a Trump-appointed federal judge in Midland, Texas, in two rulings — for the northern population on March 29, 2025, and for the endangered southern population on August 12, 2025. The delistings benefited the Permian Basin Petroleum Association and National Cattlemen's Beef Association, who argued conservation easements were sufficient, ending requirements for energy companies and ranchers to protect the birds' mating grounds across the southern Great Plains.

title: Trump Media Raises $2.5 Billion from ~50 Institutional Investors for Bitcoin Treasury
synopsis: On May 27, 2025, Trump Media & Technology Group — the parent company of Truth Social, of which Donald Trump owns just over 50 percent — announced it would raise $2.5 billion from approximately 50 institutional investors: $1.5 billion in stock at the last closing price and $1 billion in convertible bonds, to build a Bitcoin Treasury. Trump, as controlling shareholder, stood to directly benefit from any appreciation in DJT stock triggered by the capital raise and Bitcoin strategy. The deal was announced less than two weeks after Trump's Middle East trip, during which Gulf sovereign wealth funds and crypto-adjacent entities were central participants in investment forums. The transaction deepened concerns that Trump's personal financial stake in Truth Social created ongoing incentives to promote crypto-friendly regulation, tax treatment, and foreign investment flows into entities he controlled.

title: Mar-a-Lago Membership Raised to $1 Million as Access to the President Becomes Marketable
synopsis: Trump raised Mar-a-Lago's initiation fee to $1 million per membership in late 2024 — a 43 percent increase from $700,000 — explicitly timed ahead of his return to the presidency. The club, capped at approximately 500 members, offers direct physical access to Trump and visiting dignitaries in an unvetted social setting; during Trump's first term, members influenced policy through informal access and memos scrawled on cocktail napkins. Annual dues run approximately $22,750 atop the initiation fee, generating an estimated $24 million or more annually. Ethics watchdogs noted that the club's membership structure functionally sells proximity to the presidency at a price set by the president himself, with no disclosure requirements for who is buying memberships or what they are seeking from the administration.

title: RFK Jr. Cites Fraudulent Vaccine-Autism Paper at Senate Confirmation Hearing
synopsis: During his January 29–30, 2025 Senate HELP Committee confirmation hearing for HHS Secretary, Robert F. Kennedy Jr. refused to state that vaccines do not cause autism, despite overwhelming scientific consensus. When Republican Chairman Sen. Bill Cassidy of Louisiana presented a 2014 meta-analysis of 1.2 million children finding zero vaccine-autism link, Kennedy deflected, then cited a fatally flawed January 2025 paper by researcher Mawson published in Science, Public Health Policy and the Law — a journal not indexed on PubMed or MEDLINE. The study claimed vaccinated Florida Medicaid children were 2.7 times more likely to develop autism, but epidemiologists identified severe confounding, ignored all contra-evidence, and noted it cited a previously retracted paper. Kennedy declared he would follow the science while citing junk science. The original 1998 Wakefield study that sparked vaccine-autism concerns had already been retracted as fraudulent. Cassidy stated he was struggling with Kennedy's nomination before ultimately voting to confirm him. The episode signaled Kennedy's intent to use HHS to promote long-debunked anti-vaccine theories as official policy.

title: White House Systematically Deploys AI Deepfakes as Official Government Communications
synopsis: Beginning in early 2025, the Trump White House formally adopted AI-generated deepfakes and synthetic media as standard government communications tools. PolitiFact's October 2025 analysis documented 36 AI posts from Trump's Truth Social since inauguration, with the White House X account and DHS also regularly publishing AI-fabricated imagery. Content included: an AI fake of Nancy Pelosi falsely claiming to admit insider trading crimes (September 8, 2025); a deepfake of Democratic Rep. Hakeem Jeffries and Sen. Chuck Schumer in sombreros with fake audio (September 29, 2025, reshared 19,400 times); Trump as pope after Francis's death; a cartoon of Trump firing Fed Chair Jerome Powell; and a video of Trump dumping feces on protesters. Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt defended the practice, stating Trump's sharing of AI content was quite refreshing. When asked about an actual White House maintenance video, Trump falsely attributed it to AI, then mused if something happens really bad, maybe I'll have to just blame AI. The White House posted on X on July 11, 2025: Nowhere in the Constitution does it say we can't post banger memes. The memes will continue. House Speaker Mike Johnson defended the practice as satire.

title: Schedule F Reinstated to Politicize 50,000 Civil Service Positions
synopsis: On January 21, 2025, Trump reinstated Schedule F (renamed Schedule Policy/Career) via executive order, beginning the process of reclassifying up to 50,000 federal employees from protected civil servants to at-will workers dismissable at the president's direction. The change targeted policy-influencing positions, covering career professionals in national security, regulatory, and law enforcement roles. The executive order explicitly stated that employees must faithfully implement administration policies and that failure to do so was grounds for dismissal — effectively requiring political compliance rather than professional performance as a condition of employment. The merit-based civil service system, established after the Pendleton Civil Service Reform Act of 1883 to eliminate politically corrupt patronage hiring, was built precisely to prevent this kind of presidential control. Critics including the American Federation of Government Employees noted the order would allow mass replacement of experienced nonpartisan professionals with political loyalists.

title: Trump Broad Assertion of Inherent Presidential Power to Override Federal Law
synopsis: Across dozens of executive orders issued in January and February 2025, legal scholars Adam Cox and Trevor Morrison documented that Trump was asserting an unprecedented constitutional theory: that the president holds inherent authority to override, disregard, or suspend Acts of Congress when they conflict with his policy agenda. The orders covered immigration, TikTok, energy, birthright citizenship, and more — each relying on claims of inherent executive power that went beyond existing statutes or directly contradicted them. In the TikTok order, Trump instructed the Attorney General not to enforce an Act of Congress for 75 days because the law interfered with his ability to act. In immigration orders, Trump claimed invasion authority allowed him to suspend the entire immigration statutory code. Stanford Law Review published an analysis in July 2025 finding the administration had advanced practical and statutory arguments inflected with constitutional considerations suggesting Article II gave the president a preclusive presidential impoundment prerogative. Courts repeatedly rejected the theory while acknowledging the Supreme Court had not yet rendered a definitive ruling.

title: Kilmar Abrego Garcia: Wrongful Deportation to CECOT, Supreme Court Defied
synopsis: Kilmar Armando Abrego Garcia, a Salvadoran national living in Maryland with his wife and children and no criminal record, was arrested and deported on March 15, 2025, to El Salvador's CECOT prison in defiance of a 2019 immigration court order explicitly prohibiting his removal to El Salvador due to risk of gang persecution. The U.S. government acknowledged the deportation was an administrative error. The Supreme Court unanimously ruled April 10, 2025, that the administration must facilitate his return. Rather than comply, the Trump administration stonewalled, with Judge Paula Xinis ruling in April 2025 that the administration's refusal to answer questions reflects a willful and bad faith refusal to comply with discovery obligations. President Trump publicly stated he wanted to bypass due process. Abrego Garcia was held at CECOT for nearly three months before being returned to the U.S. in June 2025 — not to resume his immigration case, but to face new criminal human trafficking charges the administration filed. A federal judge continued to find unresolved compliance issues in July 2025.

title: Third-Country Asylum Deportations: 17,500 Asylum Seekers Sent to Nations They Have Never Visited
synopsis: By May 2026, approximately 17,500 people had been deported to third countries — nations other than their home country — under Trump's unprecedented asylum cancellation campaign, per Third Country Deportation Watch. ICE attorneys filed over 24,000 motions in immigration court to pretermit active asylum cases by routing claimants to countries they had no connection to — including Ecuador, Honduras, Guatemala, and Uganda. In one documented case, a Russian national and her 4-year-old child were ordered deported to Uganda. An Iranian national detained since December 2024 received a motion to deport him to Uganda four days before his scheduled asylum hearing. In November 2025, the Board of Immigration Appeals ruled immigration judges must decide third-country deportation before reviewing asylum claims, effectively placing the burden on asylum-seekers to prove they fear persecution in countries they've never seen. Roughly 12,300 people withdrew or abandoned asylum claims after receiving a pretermission motion — a 16% abandonment rate. Honduras had only agreed to accept 10 non-Honduran deportees per month, yet over 6,300 non-Hondurans received Honduras deportation orders.

title: Trump Signs EO 14248 Requiring Citizenship Proof to Register to Vote
synopsis: On March 25, 2025, President Trump signed Executive Order 14248, Preserving and Protecting the Integrity of American Elections, requiring documentary proof of U.S. citizenship — such as a passport or REAL ID — to register to vote using the federal voter registration form. The order also directed DHS and DOGE to review state voter rolls against federal immigration databases, threatened to withhold federal election funding from non-compliant states, and ordered the DOJ to enforce Election Day ballot-receipt deadlines against 18 states that allow postmarked-by-Election-Day mail ballots. The Brennan Center estimated 21.3 million eligible citizens lacked ready access to qualifying documents. Federal courts repeatedly blocked the order's major provisions. U.S. District Judge Denise Casper permanently enjoined most of the order in June 2026, finding Trump lacked constitutional authority over election procedures reserved to Congress and the states. Colorado Secretary of State Jena Griswold called the order unlawful weaponization of federal power designed to make it harder for voters to push back at the ballot box.

title: SAVE Program Weaponized to Flag 67 Million Voter Registrations as Suspect
synopsis: By May 2026, the Trump administration had run at least 67 million voter registrations — primarily from Republican-controlled states that agreed to share data — through a dramatically expanded version of the DHS Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements (SAVE) program. Originally designed to verify immigration status for benefits programs, SAVE was overhauled in spring 2025 to enable bulk scanning of state voter rolls against federal citizenship databases. The expanded system flagged tens of thousands of registrations as potential noncitizens or deceased persons, with some states then suspending those voters' eligibility with as little as 30 days to respond. The nonpartisan Institute for Responsive Government noted that historically 16% of SAVE searches required manual verification, meaning hundreds of thousands of legitimate citizens could face erroneous flags. A federal judge blocked the modified SAVE tool in June 2026. Maine Secretary of State Shenna Bellows said DHS told her it planned to retain all uploaded state voter data for 10 years for audit purposes, raising concerns about a de facto federal voter database built through the backdoor.

title: Trump Signs EO 14399 Creating National Voter List and USPS Mail Ballot Control
synopsis: On March 31, 2026, Trump signed Executive Order 14399, Ensuring Citizenship Verification and Integrity in Federal Elections, directing DHS and the SSA to compile a federal State Citizenship List for each state and giving the U.S. Postal Service unprecedented authority to bar delivery of mail ballots to anyone not pre-approved on a state list submitted 60 days before the election. The order directed USPS rulemaking to require unique barcoded envelopes for all mail ballots. Election experts said no USPS rulemaking could realistically be completed before November 2026 and that the pre-approval list requirement conflicted with state laws in most states. Election law expert Rick Hasen called it unconstitutional and impossible to implement in time. Twenty-four states immediately threatened litigation. Wisconsin Elections Commission chair Ann Jacobs warned the pre-approval list could disenfranchise voters who move before elections. Arizona Secretary of State Adrian Fontes called it a disgusting overreach.

title: DHS Uses Federal Disaster Grants to Coerce States on Election Changes
synopsis: In June 2026, the Trump administration announced that Federal Emergency Management Agency and DHS homeland security grants would be conditioned on states adopting a sweeping set of election changes, including phasing out electronic voting systems in favor of hand-marked paper ballots, running voter rolls through the SAVE citizenship verification database, and verifying citizenship of all election workers. States that refused would lose up to 20% of FEMA antiterrorism grant funding. More than two dozen states filed suit in Rhode Island federal court in July 2026, arguing the administration was unconstitutionally coercing states into relinquishing control over their elections. Rhode Island Attorney General Peter Neronha said the administration was using the safety of Americans as collateral. Election experts noted that some required changes — such as adopting entirely new voting systems — were logistically impossible before November 2026 elections even for states that wanted to comply.

title: DOJ Demands All 2024 Wayne County Michigan Ballots in Swing State Power Play
synopsis: On April 14, 2026, Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon sent a letter to Wayne County, Michigan — home to Detroit and nearly 865,000 votes cast in 2024 — demanding that the county turn over all 2024 election ballots, ballot receipts, and ballot envelopes within 14 days, threatening court action for non-compliance. The request cited the Civil Rights Act of 1960 but justified the demand using fraud allegations from the 2020 election, even though the request was for 2024 records from an election Trump won. Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel vowed to fight the demand, and county officials noted the county did not actually hold custody of the ballots. FBI Director Kash Patel said the DOJ was probing past elections and could soon make arrests, amplifying the intimidation. The Wayne County demand came weeks after the FBI seized 700 boxes of 2020 Fulton County, Georgia, ballots and subpoenaed 2020 records from Maricopa County, Arizona. Legal experts described the escalating demands as a coordinated strategy to intimidate election workers in heavily Democratic, majority-minority counties in swing states ahead of the 2026 midterms.

title: Kash Patel Uses FBI to Investigate Trump Political Enemies
synopsis: Despite pledging at his January 2025 Senate confirmation hearing that there would be no politicization at the FBI and no retributive actions, FBI Director Kash Patel — author of Government Gangsters, which included a 60-name deep state enemies list — oversaw the launch of FBI investigations against multiple political opponents named by Trump. By August 2025, reported targets included former national security adviser John Bolton, former CIA Director John Brennan (probed for allegedly lying to Congress about the Russia investigation), former FBI Director James Comey (investigated over an Instagram post), and former DHS staffer Miles Taylor. Attorney General Pam Bondi purged at least 35 DOJ employees for their Jan. 6 or classified documents work. Axios reported that the administration had targeted numerous people Trump had previously named as enemies. A White House spokesperson declined to address accusations of targeting political opponents.

title: USAID Global Journalism Funding Freeze Devastates 700+ Independent Newsrooms
synopsis: In late January 2025, the Trump administration froze all USAID foreign assistance, eliminating $268 million annually that Congress had allocated to support independent media and press freedom in more than 30 countries. USAID had supported training for 6,200 journalists and funded 707 non-state news outlets according to a factsheet the agency removed from its website after the freeze. The Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project (OCCRP) — which distributes funds globally — lost 29 percent of its 2025 budget (over $5 million), laid off 20 percent of its staff, and ended almost all grants to partner newsrooms worldwide. Russian exile media outlet Meduza, which relied on USAID intermediaries for roughly 15 percent of its budget, was thrown into financial crisis. Ukrainian media faced catastrophic exposure: the U.S. had provided 70-80 percent of all foreign media assistance to Ukraine, per the Global Forum for Media Development. Investigative outlet Slidstvo.Info saw 80 percent of its budget affected. El Salvador's Voz Publica reduced its staff from six to three journalists. Russian, Iranian, and Chinese state propaganda applauded the freeze. RSF called the action a vacuum that plays into the hands of propagandists and authoritarian states and noted it was half of global government funding for public-interest journalism worldwide.

title: U.S. Drops to 57th on 2025 World Press Freedom Index
synopsis: On May 2, 2025, Reporters Without Borders (RSF) published its 2025 World Press Freedom Index, ranking the United States 57th out of 180 countries — a drop of two additional places from its 2024 ranking, extending a slide of over 25 places in recent years. The U.S. now ranked one position behind Sierra Leone and was downgraded from satisfactory to problematic in press freedom status. RSF stated that Donald Trump's second term as president has led to an alarming deterioration in press freedom, indicative of an authoritarian shift in government. The economic indicator for U.S. press freedom had fallen more than 14 points in two years. Over 60 percent of journalists surveyed in Arizona, Florida, Nevada, and Pennsylvania said it was difficult to earn a living wage as a journalist, and 75 percent said their outlet struggles for economic viability. The U.S. Press Freedom Tracker recorded more than 170 attacks on journalists in 2025 — nearly double the previous year — driven by increased violence at protests and law enforcement confrontations. RSF cited Trump's efforts to censor government data, dismantle public broadcasters, weaponize regulatory agencies, halt international media freedom aid, and sue disfavored outlets as the primary drivers of the decline.

title: Operation Midnight Hammer: US Bombs Iran Nuclear Sites
synopsis: On June 21, 2025, President Trump ordered Operation Midnight Hammer, the first-ever direct US military attack on Iran. Seven B-2 Spirit stealth bombers flew 18 hours from Whiteman Air Force Base, Missouri, using mid-air refueling and a Pacific-bound decoy fleet to deceive Iranian air defenses. The bombers dropped 14 GBU-57 Massive Ordnance Penetrator 30,000-pound bunker-buster bombs on the Fordo and Natanz nuclear enrichment facilities; a submarine launched Tomahawk cruise missiles at the Isfahan site. Over 125 US aircraft participated in total. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth called Trump from Bedminster and obtained final authorization hours before impact. Trump watched the mission from the White House Situation Room alongside VP JD Vance, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, and Joint Chiefs Chairman Gen. Dan Caine. Trump declared the strikes a spectacular military success in a televised address, warning Iran: There will be either peace or there will be tragedy. The UN called the strikes a dangerous escalation. Congress had not authorized the use of military force against Iran.

title: Operation Rough Rider: 52-Day Yemen Bombing Campaign
synopsis: On March 15, 2025, Trump launched Operation Rough Rider against Houthi forces in Yemen, the largest US military operation in the Middle East since he took office. Over 52 days through May 5, US forces struck more than 1,100 Houthi targets using two aircraft carrier strike groups — USS Harry S. Truman and USS Carl Vinson — killing hundreds of fighters and several senior commanders. The US lost two F/A-18 Super Hornets worth approximately $67 million each and seven MQ-9 Reaper drones valued at over $200 million total; total operation costs exceeded $2 billion. A strike on a migrant detention center in Sanaa killed dozens of civilians, and a separate strike on an oil terminal killed 68 African migrants. US intelligence ultimately assessed the Houthis had suffered some degradation but could easily reconstitute. The campaign ended with a ceasefire mediated by Oman on May 6 in which the Houthis agreed only not to target US-flagged vessels — leaving Israeli shipping and commercial Red Sea traffic still vulnerable.

title: Trump Berates and Expels Zelensky from Oval Office
synopsis: On February 28, 2025, in an extraordinary public confrontation without precedent in modern US diplomatic history, President Trump and Vice President JD Vance berated Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky during a White House meeting intended to finalize a rare-earth minerals agreement and coordinate Ukraine war strategy. Trump raised his voice repeatedly, telling Zelensky You're gambling with World War III and You don't have the cards right now. Vance accused Zelensky of being disrespectful and demanded he simply say thank you. The confrontation erupted when Zelensky pushed back on Trump's push for rapid concessions to Russia and suggested the US did not understand the consequences of appeasing Putin. Trump, who had previously called Zelensky a dictator without elections, ultimately had the Ukrainian president ejected from the White House early. A planned joint press conference was canceled, the rare-earth minerals deal went unsigned, and Secretary of State Marco Rubio publicly demanded Zelensky apologize. Republican Senator Lindsey Graham called it a complete, utter disaster.

title: Maximum Pressure Iran: Oil Sanctions and Shadow Fleet Targeting
synopsis: On February 4, 2025, Trump signed National Security Presidential Memorandum NSPM-2 reinstating a comprehensive maximum pressure campaign against Iran, directing the Treasury Department to drive Iranian oil exports to zero and sanctioning all participants in Iran's shadow oil tanker fleet. By April 2025, OFAC had sanctioned over 86 individuals and entities across 25 countries and blocked 98 tankers involved in shipping Iranian oil. The administration conducted four successive rounds of Iran oil sanctions within the first 60 days, including the first-ever US designation of a Chinese teapot refinery processing Iranian crude. Treasury issued comprehensive guidance warning global shipping companies, insurers, and port operators of sanctions exposure. Iran responded by accelerating uranium enrichment and expanding the shadow fleet through alternative registries. Critics noted the blanket sanctions disproportionately hurt civilian populations while Iran's nuclear program accelerated, rendering the pressure campaign's strategic logic counterproductive ahead of the eventual military strikes.

title: US Withdraws from 66 International Organizations in Mass Exit
synopsis: On January 7, 2026, Trump signed an executive memorandum withdrawing the United States from 66 international organizations, conventions, and treaties following a review by Secretary of State Marco Rubio. The mass withdrawal included the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change — the treaty underpinning all international climate agreements — and the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, the world's leading authority on climate science. Additional withdrawals covered the International Solar Alliance, the International Institute for Democracy and Electoral Assistance, the Global Counter-Terrorism Forum, the UN Register of Conventional Arms, and dozens of other multilateral bodies. Nearly half of the 66 entities were UN-affiliated. The White House stated the organizations no longer serve American interests and promote ineffective or hostile agendas, including radical climate policies, global governance and ideological programs that conflict with US sovereignty. Constitutional scholars noted that many of these were multilateral bodies established by Senate-ratified treaties, raising questions about whether Trump had unilateral authority to exit.

title: US-Iran Ceasefire Collapses: Exchanges of Strikes Over Strait of Hormuz
synopsis: Following the June 21, 2025 US bombing of Iranian nuclear sites, the two nations engaged in months of escalating conflict before a 14-point Memorandum of Understanding was signed on June 17, 2026, intended to reopen the Strait of Hormuz — through which 20% of the world's oil transits. The ceasefire collapsed within days when Iran targeted commercial ships it deemed to be using unauthorized navigation routes. On June 25–27, 2026, after Iranian IRGC forces attacked the Singapore-flagged MV Ever Lovely cargo ship, the US launched waves of retaliatory strikes on Iranian coastal defense sites, missile storage facilities, and radar systems. Iran retaliated with ballistic missiles and drones targeting US military infrastructure in Kuwait and at the Fifth Naval Fleet in Bahrain. Both sides accused the other of ceasefire violations. Trump warned on Truth Social there may come a point when we are no longer able to be reasonable. The Strait of Hormuz was effectively closed at points during the conflict, causing global oil price spikes and threatening international shipping.

title: North Korea Rejects Denuclearization, Demands US Accept Nuclear Reality
synopsis: On July 28–29, 2025, North Korea's Kim Yo Jong — believed to speak for her brother, Supreme Leader Kim Jong Un — publicly dismissed US hopes for denuclearization talks, stating that no future dialogue would end North Korea's nuclear weapons program. Responding to Trump's repeated overtures for a summit, Kim Yo Jong conceded that the personal relationship between Kim and Trump is not bad, but warned that any attempt to use personal diplomacy to end the nuclear program would only be subject of mockery. She demanded the US accept the changed reality. North Korea had entered 2025 with Kim ordering increased production of weapons-grade nuclear material in January; analysts estimated Pyongyang had enough material for up to 90 warheads. Trump expressed desire to meet Kim this year while simultaneously maintaining a stated goal of complete denuclearization — a position Kim had explicitly rejected as impossible. Meanwhile, North Korea had deepened its military and diplomatic ties with Russia, including deploying troops to support Russian forces in Ukraine, giving Pyongyang new geopolitical leverage the Trump administration was unable to effectively counter.

title: Marko Elez Given Admin Write-Access to $5.4T Federal Payment System
synopsis: On February 1, 2025, the day after Treasury career official David Lebryk was placed on administrative leave for resisting DOGE, 25-year-old Marko Elez — a former SpaceX and X employee with no government or finance experience — was granted read and write access to the Bureau of the Fiscal Service's Payment Automation Manager (PAM) and Secure Payment System (SPS). These two systems processed $5.45 trillion in federal payments in fiscal year 2024, including Social Security checks, tax refunds, veterans' pay, and federal salaries. White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent repeatedly told Congress and the press that DOGE's access was read-only. Treasury officials actually altered internal records to indicate Elez no longer had write access before senior IT staff stated it was rescinded. Reporting by Wired and Talking Points Memo confirmed Elez had already made extensive changes to the code base for the payment systems. His write access was not revoked until February 5, the day a federal judge issued a temporary restraining order. Five former Treasury Secretaries warned in a New York Times op-ed that DOGE had put America's payments system and the highly sensitive data within it to the risk of exposure, potentially to our adversaries.

title: DOGE Bypassed Security Protocols on Three Treasury Payment Systems, GAO Finds
synopsis: A Government Accountability Office audit released in April 2026 confirmed that two DOGE associates gained access to Bureau of the Fiscal Service (BFS) payment systems from January 20 through April 11, 2025, without following proper IT security protocols. The GAO found that one DOGE employee could view, copy, and print data from three BFS systems, and was inadvertently granted temporary access to create, modify, and delete data for one system. The staffer sent personally identifiable information on 350 USAID payment recipients to another DOGE staffer via an unencrypted Excel file using a Treasury email, then forwarded the unencrypted file to two DOGE members at the General Services Administration without approval. The BFS had not implemented all required cybersecurity controls. One DOGE staffer left the agency while still holding an interim security clearance enabling access to multiple BFS systems, because BFS never conducted an exit interview or obtained post-employment protection documentation. The GAO issued six recommendations for remediation. Treasury agreed with only three. The watchdog concluded that payment data remained at a greater risk of improper access, modification, disclosure, or misuse until proper controls were established.

title: DOGE Fires 400 FAA Workers During Active Aviation Safety Crisis
synopsis: On the night of February 14-15, 2025, the Trump administration fired hundreds of Federal Aviation Administration probationary employees via email — just three weeks after a U.S. Army Black Hawk helicopter collided with an American Airlines CRJ700 near Reagan National Airport, killing all 67 people aboard. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy confirmed fewer than 400 were let go, claiming no air traffic controllers or safety-critical personnel were terminated. The Professional Aviation Safety Specialists (PASS) union confirmed 133 of its members were fired, including aeronautical information specialists who update navigational charts, aviation safety assistants, maintenance mechanics, telecommunications specialists who maintain radar and communications infrastructure, and flight operations program specialists. PASS president David Spero called the firings unconscionable in the aftermath of three deadly aircraft accidents in the past month. The Atlantic obtained internal FAA data showing over 1,300 additional employees had expressed interest in early retirement, including in critical safety support roles. About 12 percent of aeronautical information specialists had either left or were poised to leave. The cuts eliminated the pipeline of new professionals to replace retiring workers, exacerbating a pre-existing controller staffing shortage that the NTSB had flagged as a risk factor in the Reagan Airport collision.

title: Musk's Starlink Positioned to Seize $2.4B FAA Contract He Helped Undermine
synopsis: In late February 2025, the Washington Post, AP, and Bloomberg reported that the FAA was on the cusp of canceling a $2.4 billion contract awarded to Verizon in 2023 for upgrading the nation's air traffic control communications backbone, and handing the work instead to Elon Musk's Starlink (owned by SpaceX). The existing Verizon FENS contract was designed to connect 4,600 FAA sites over 15 years. A SpaceX-led team embedded inside the FAA — several members of which had been given FAA email addresses — was the team recommending the switch. Senior FAA career officials refused to sign paperwork authorizing the contract change, so DOGE sought support from Trump-appointed acting FAA administrator Chris Rocheleau. Musk had publicly posted on X that the Verizon system was not working and posed catastrophic failure risk within single digit months — claims experts said were unsupported. The FAA itself regulated SpaceX for rocket launches and had pending civil penalty proceedings against the company. Ethics experts at Georgetown and UC Santa Clara said the arrangement was an extraordinary conflict of interest. Musk's DOGE role gave him access to FAA staffing decisions, budget cuts, and contract processes at the very agency that oversaw his private company's launches.

title: DOGE Fires 6,700 IRS Workers During Tax Season, Costing Trillions in Revenue
synopsis: On February 20, 2025, the IRS began firing approximately 6,700 probationary employees — roughly 6 percent of the agency's workforce — during the active tax-filing season. IRS Director of Talent Acquisition Christy Armstrong wept during a phone call with employees as she announced the terminations. Treasury Inspector General data confirmed that by March 2025, the IRS had lost 31 percent of its revenue agents (approximately 3,600 auditors) through firings and the deferred resignation program. Revenue agents primarily handle audits of wealthy taxpayers and corporations. The Yale Budget Lab estimated the planned reductions would cost $323 billion in lost tax revenue over the next decade, with a 50 percent workforce cut potentially costing $2.4 trillion over ten years. The cuts disproportionately targeted enforcement staff hired under the Inflation Reduction Act, which had been projected to collect hundreds of billions in additional taxes. DOGE's stated rationale was eliminating Biden-era hiring surges. Administration plans called for cutting IRS workforce by up to 40-50 percent by mid-2025.
